references.text: Addresses the punishment for striking a person so that they die and establishes the principle of capital punishment for murder.
Prohibits hating one's brother in the heart, which can lead to hidden violence against one's neighbor.
Describes various ways of killing, including lying in wait, relating to secret attacks on one's neighbor.
Saul tried to kill David in secret, an example of striking one's neighbor in hiding.
Describes the wicked who lie in ambush and kill the innocent in secret.
Refers to those who sharpen their tongue like a sword and shoot secretly at the innocent.
Warns that whoever carries guilt for bloodshed will flee to the grave—a consequence of secret murder.
Condemns those who take bribes to shed innocent blood, a form of hidden violence.
